title: GraphFLEx: Unsupervised Structure Learning $\underline{\text{F}}$ramework for $\underline{\text{L}}$arge $\underline{\text{Ex}}$panding $\underline{\text{Graph}}$s
claim: Existing structure-learning methods see compute time blow up as graphs grow; ours keeps growth near-linear at scale.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, shared axes, (a) ours vs (b) vanilla baseline
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the same axes: Number of Nodes (up to 50,000) on x and Time in Seconds (0 to 1200) on y. Both show six colored lines with markers: ANN (red), KNN (green), Log model (yellow), L2 model (blue), Empirical Covariance (orange), and Large model (purple). Panel (a), labeled GraphFLEx, has curves that stay low and roughly linear. Most finish under 400 seconds, and the red ANN line is near 50 seconds. Only the yellow and orange lines climb steeply. Panel (b), labeled Vanilla, shows the same methods without GraphFLEx. The yellow and blue lines shoot off the top of the chart within a few thousand nodes. Orange grows convexly and exits the top near 40K nodes. Red and purple end near 450-500 seconds. The eye goes first to the steep curves in (b), which contrast with the flatter curves in (a).
caption: High computational time required to learn graph structures using existing methods, whereas GraphFLEx effectively controls computational growth, achieving near-linear scalability. Notably, Vanilla KNN failed to construct graph structures for more than 10K nodes due to memory limitations.
abstract: Graph structure learning is a core problem in graph-based machine learning, essential for uncovering latent relationships and ensuring model interpretability. However, most existing approaches are ill-suited for large-scale and dynamically evolving graphs, as they often require complete re-learning of the structure upon the arrival of new nodes and incur substantial computational and memory costs. In this work, we propose GraphFLEx—a unified and scalable framework for Graph Structure Learning in Large and Expanding Graphs. GraphFLEx mitigates the scalability bottlenecks by restricting edge formation to structurally relevant subsets of nodes identified through a combination of clustering and coarsening techniques. This dramatically reduces the search space and enables efficient, incremental graph updates. The framework supports 48 flexible configurations by integrating diverse choices of learning paradigms, coarsening strategies, and clustering methods, making it adaptable to a wide range of graph settings and learning objectives. Extensive experiments across 26 diverse datasets and graph neural network architectures demonstrate that GraphFLEx achieves state-of-the-art performance with significantly improved scalability. Our implementation is publicly available here: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Scaling Graph Learning-CB67/README.md.
